issues.legal_issue: A possession decree in a landlord-tenant suit cannot be entered on admissions alone when the tenant raises a material and plausible defense based on agreements to sell that requires evidentiary determination.
material_facts: The suit sought possession on the basis of a landlord-tenant relationship. The parties did not dispute the lease agreements, the rent terms, or that rent had not been paid after the extended lease expired.
The tenant relied on several agreements to sell and contended that the sale arrangements and related adjustments changed the parties’ relationship and addressed the accrued rent.
The dispute over the agreements and the tenant’s defense had not been tested by evidence; a suit for specific performance was also pending.
issues.conclusion: The admissions were not clear and categorical enough to justify a possession decree without considering the defense. The decree was set aside and the suit remitted for trial, with an opportunity for the parties to lead evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XII Rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court has discretionary power to enter judgment on admissions, but should exercise it only where the admissions are specific, clear and categorical. Admissions of a landlord-tenant relationship do not by themselves warrant a decree where a material defense requires appreciation of evidence. The Court applied S.M. Asif v. Virendar Kumar Bajaj (2015) 9 SCC 287, and considered the principles in Himani Alloys Ltd. v. Tata Steel Ltd. (2011) 15 SCC 273 and Hari Steel and General Industries Ltd. v. Daljit Singh (2019) 20 SCC 425 concerning the discretionary nature of the power and the need for clear admissions.

rule.if: possession_suit_based_on_tenancy and tenancy_admitted and lease_terms_admitted and sale_agreements_form_material_defense and defense_requires_evidence

predicates.possession_suit_based_on_tenancy: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking possession on the basis of a landlord-tenant relationship.
predicates.tenancy_admitted: The tenant admitted the existence of the landlord-tenant relationship.
predicates.lease_terms_admitted: The parties did not dispute the lease agreements or their rent terms.
predicates.sale_agreements_form_material_defense: The tenant relied on agreements to sell as a defense affecting the parties’ relationship or the rent claim.
predicates.defense_requires_evidence: The defense’s contents and legal effect had not been established and required the parties to lead evidence.

issues.definition: When a possession suit is based on an admitted tenancy and lease terms but a material defense based on sale agreements requires evidence, the admissions alone cannot support a possession decree, and the case must proceed to trial.

issues.legal_issue: In a landlord-tenant suit where the lease rent terms and non-payment are admitted, the trial court may require payment of arrears and deposit of ongoing rent while the suit is pending.
material_facts: The parties did not dispute the lease agreements, the rent terms, or the stipulated rent increase under the extended lease.
The tenant had not paid rent after the extended lease expired.

The Court remitted the possession suit for trial and directed the trial court first to determine the monthly rent applying the stipulated increase and make appropriate orders for arrears and regular rent deposits; payment was subject to the outcomes of the possession suit and the specific-performance suit.
issues.conclusion: The trial court was directed to determine the monthly rent using the stipulated year-to-year increase and make appropriate orders for payment of arrears and deposit of regular monthly rent, subject to the outcomes of the two suits.
issues.legal_principle: In a suit based on a landlord-tenant relationship, rent and arrears should be paid in accordance with the court’s order. The Court relied on S.M. Asif v. Virendar Kumar Bajaj (2015) 9 SCC 287 and applied the admitted lease terms and rent increase in directing the trial court to address payment pending the suit.

rule.if: possession_suit_based_on_tenancy and lease_rent_terms_admitted and rent_unpaid and rent_increase_stipulated

predicates.possession_suit_based_on_tenancy: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking possession on the basis of a landlord-tenant relationship.
predicates.lease_rent_terms_admitted: The parties did not dispute the lease agreements or their rent terms.
predicates.rent_unpaid: The tenant had not paid rent due under the lease.
predicates.rent_increase_stipulated: The lease terms provided for an increase in rent over time.

issues.definition: When a possession suit is based on tenancy, the rent terms and an increase are admitted, and rent remains unpaid, the tenant must pay arrears and deposit ongoing rent while the suit is pending.
